'''Robert Henry Sorgenfrey''' (August 14, 1915 – January 7, 1996) was an American [[mathematician]] and Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] at UCLA until his retirement in 1979.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.senate.ucla.edu/FormsDocs/Emeriti/sample-stmts.htm |title=Robert Sorgenfrey |website=www.senate.ucla.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000824085429/http://www.senate.ucla.edu/FormsDocs/Emeriti/sample-stmts.htm |archive-date=2000-08-24}} </ref> The [[Sorgenfrey line]] and the [[Sorgenfrey plane]] are named after him; the Sorgenfrey line was the first example of a [[normal space|normal]] [[topological space]] whose product with itself is not normal.
